sections.heading: Crash duties and animal hazards
sections.markdown:
## Crash duties and animal hazards

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A01
After involvement in a crash, stop at once in a safe location. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A01
The handbook requires immediate notice to the nearest law-enforcement agency when a crash causes injury or death, or property damage exceeding 500 dollars. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A01
Provide reasonable assistance to an injured person after a crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A01
Warn approaching traffic only when doing so does not put you or others at risk; use hazard lamps if possible and reflective triangles when available. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A01
Exchange the driver's name, address, plate number and license number with others involved in the crash, and obtain the corresponding information from the other driver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A01
If you damage a vehicle with nobody attending it, locate its owner or leave a note where that owner can readily find it. Include your contact name and address plus the name of your vehicle's owner. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A01
Do not assume someone is uninjured merely because the person says so; seek professional assistance promptly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A01
Avoid unnecessary movement of an injured person, since unskilled handling may worsen an injury. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A01
After a crash on a multilane highway or expressway with no apparent serious injury or death, drivers must move the involved vehicles to a safe refuge when the vehicles can be driven normally and safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A01
Move a crash vehicle only if doing so will not create further danger or harm to people, the vehicles or the roadway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A01
If a crash participant cannot move the vehicle, that person may ask a nearby driver with a valid license of the appropriate class to move it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A01
Moving a vehicle to safety under the described crash rule does not by itself establish fault or eliminate the driver's duties to stop and provide information. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A01
A driver who moves a crash vehicle under the safety rule retains the ability to file a written report with the local police agency. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=51]

Misconceptions: Moving a vehicle to the safe refuge described by the rule does not alone establish fault; seeing one deer does not establish that the road is clear behind it.
Mnemonic: Stop, protect, report, exchange, then move only if safe.
Glossary: A safe refuge is a location off the traveled roadway suitable for the vehicle under the described conditions; an unattended vehicle still has an owner who must receive the required information.
Dynamic-fact isolation: Reporting thresholds, civil immunity, medical procedures, wildlife statistics and insurance practices remain dated-source review.

ranked.label: Protect the scene without added danger
Move a vehicle only under safe conditions

corpus_stability.reason: Revision frequency and legal-currentness are not independently established; retain release hold while authoring the dated source-grounded candidate.

verification_debt.claim_text: The dated handbook facts retain source freshness, rights and independent factual-review debt; no current-law equivalence or live service/fee policy is certified.
The property-damage reporting threshold requires current legal confirmation; no current reporting-law clearance is asserted.
Bleeding-control, warming and injured-person handling procedures beyond avoiding unnecessary movement require clinical/safety review and are withheld.
The broad Good Samaritan civil-immunity sentence lacks complete legal conditions; no blanket immunity is authored.
Fixed deer-crash percentages, exact seasonal claims, headlight-blinking/horn deterrence effectiveness and insurer-report requirements require current evidence and are withheld.
